text:
lei: quick heads-up — after the 2.3.1 rollout i'm seeing long-context jobs (30k+ tokens) where KV memory steadily climbs and we eventually hit OOM on 48G instances. reproducible on canary.
sam: ugh. any idea if it's eviction thrash or slot leak?
jordan: profile attached from a repro run on gtx48-canary. main observation: kernel selector prefers fp16 matmul kernels for attention fallback when int8 path misses, which ends up allocating full BF16 scratch for some kernels. Result: +6GB peak vs pure int8 path.
lei: yeah that matches my trace. evict log shows repeated page churn: same slot id moved to cold pool then back within ~2s. looks like fragmentation + small-window reuse.
olivia: paste of trimmed perf log: ```
KV_REUSE_HIT 0.62
KV_EVICTIONS 182
KV_PREFETCH_MISS 0.14
MEM_PEAK_GB 41.8
MEM_BASELINE_INT8_GB 35.2
LAT_P50_MS 23.4
LAT_P95_MS 89.1
ACCURACY_DELTA_TOPP0.9 -0.8%
```
sam: interesting that accuracy drop is small but consistent on int8 path; could be quant noise from the slots that survive eviction cycles and get partially re-quantized?
jordan: possibly. also saw kernel-selector logs: "selected_kernel=attn_fp16_fallback reason=missing_int8_kernel for seqlen>2048" — so for longer windows we're switching to fp16 kernels which expand KV page size. Need to confirm whether the fallback inflates per-slot metadata too.
lei: reproduction steps i used: run longctx-sim --model reranker-7b --quant=int8 --seq=32000 --concurrency=4 --batcher=adaptive. let it run 15 minutes. attached command output.
ci-bot: deploy canary build redwood/runtime:v2.3.2-ks-fix started at 2149998895
olivia: i dug into slab allocator metrics — fragmentation metric shows many small free ranges (<16KB) in hot pool, seems caused by mixed-size slot writes when fallback happens mid-stream. that prevents coalescing and increases total reserved pages.
sam: two axes: 1) kernel-selection: prefer int8-compatible kernels for long ctx (if acceptable perf), add a hard limit to avoid fp16 fallback inflating KV size; 2) KV allocator: add aggressive coalesce pass on eviction or a relocate-to-large-slot policy.
jordan: agree. for (1) we can update kernel selector heuristics: if quant_profile == int8 and estimated_accuracy_loss < 1% and memory budget low then force_int8_path=true. i can prototype selector patch.
lei: for (2) i can add metric kv.fragment_coalesce_runs and a background coalesce worker that consolidates adjacent free pages every N evictions; should reduce fragmentation by ~20-30% in my sim.
olivia: also propose prefetch policy tweak: when we detect repeated small reuses (reuse_rate>0.5 within 5s) promote slot to pinned hot tier to avoid repeated cold->hot churn.
sam: sounds good. can we run an A/B canary with: kernel-fallback disabled + coalesce worker enabled + promote policy? measure memory and accuracy.
jordan: i'll push ks prototype branch and metrics. expectation: MEM_PEAK drop ~4-6GB, KV_EVICTIONS drop >40%, latency stable +/-5%, accuracy delta stays ~ -0.8 to -0.5%.
lei: i'll wire up the coalesce worker and stress test. timeline: test build by EOD, canary tomorrow.
olivia: note: need to add a regression alert on accuracy drift for quantized longctx routes (threshold 1%) and a memory growth alert on sustained increase >3GB over 10min.
ci-bot: canary pipeline completed for redwood/runtime:v2.3.2-ks-fix at 2149998915 — tests green.
sam: cool. action items: jordan -> kernel selector PR, lei -> coalesce worker + metrics, olivia -> promote policy + alerts. i'll own the canary run and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
lei: thanks, will post perf graphs and flamegraphs once tests run.
jordan: FYI i also captured a tiny patch that ensures quantized page headers don't get duplicated on fallback; that saved ~128KB per slot in my run.
olivia: small wins add up. will track end-to-end for next 48h.
sam: great teamwork — keep updates short in this thread. if we hit a regression, rollback to v2.3.1 immediately.
